raw_findings.body: `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user)` returns `Optional.empty()` and `credentialModelOpt.get()` throws `NoSuchElementException` while rendering the LOGIN_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES_INPUT page, producing a server error instead of the login form.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Runtime NoSuchElementException during form rendering for federated users, blocking login.
raw_findings.impact: `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user)` returns `Optional.empty()` and `credentialModelOpt.get()` throws `NoSuchElementException` while rendering the LOGIN_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES_INPUT page, producing a server error instead of the login form.
raw_findings.root_cause: The lookup was widened to federated storage (which can legitimately return no credential when the provider does not implement getCredentials) but the result is still dereferenced with an unguarded Optional.get().
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Handle the empty case explicitly, e.g. `credentialModelOpt.map(RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel::createFromCredentialModel)` and fall back to a defined codeNumber / throw a descriptive exception, instead of calling `Optional.get()` unconditionally.
raw_findings.title: Unchecked Optional.get() on recovery-codes credential in login bean
raw_findings.trigger: A federated user whose user-storage provider implements CredentialInputValidator/CredentialInputUpdater for `recovery-authn-codes` (so `isConfiguredFor` is true and the recovery-code form is shown) but leaves the *default* `CredentialInputUpdater.getCredentials()` implementation returning an empty stream, and has no local credential of that type.

raw_findings.body: `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues` never sets an id, so the exposed credential has a null id: it can never be matched for deletion, and `removeStoredCredentialById(recoveryCodeCredentialModel.getId())` in the authenticator would be invoked with null.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Credential returned from federated storage is unidentifiable, breaking id-based lookup/deletion paths.
raw_findings.impact: `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues` never sets an id, so the exposed credential has a null id: it can never be matched for deletion, and `removeStoredCredentialById(recoveryCodeCredentialModel.getId())` in the authenticator would be invoked with null.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new getCredentials() implementation rebuilds a credential model from raw values and drops the stored credential id.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: After building the model call `model.setId(myUser.recoveryCodes.getId())` (the id generated in `updateCredential`) before adding it to the returned list.
raw_findings.title: Federated recovery-codes credential is returned without an id
raw_findings.trigger: Any caller of `getFederatedCredentialsStream()` for a user whose recovery codes live in this storage, e.g. listing/deleting credentials in the account console (`CredentialDeleteHelper` filters federated credentials with `credentialId.equals(c.getId())`).

raw_findings.body: The following `authenticatedUser.credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById(...)` targets the local credential store only, so the exhausted federated credential is never removed while the required action is added; the stale credential keeps being reported as configured by the user-storage provider.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Silent no-op deletion leaving an exhausted credential in user storage.
raw_findings.impact: The following `authenticatedUser.credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById(...)` targets the local credential store only, so the exhausted federated credential is never removed while the required action is added; the stale credential keeps being reported as configured by the user-storage provider.
raw_findings.root_cause: The credential lookup was switched to include federated credentials without adapting the subsequent local-store removal call.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Only call `removeStoredCredentialById` when the credential came from local storage; for federated credentials delegate removal to the provider (e.g. `credentialManager().disableCredentialType(RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE)`), or make `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential` report the origin.
raw_findings.title: Exhausted federated recovery-codes credential removed via local-store API
raw_findings.trigger: A user whose recovery-codes credential is stored in a user-storage provider that consumes codes, logging in with the last remaining code so that `allCodesUsed()` becomes true.

raw_findings.body: NullPointerException on `myUser.recoveryCodes`, aborting credential listing, whereas the sibling methods `getDisableableCredentialTypesStream` and `isConfiguredFor` guard with `myUser == null`.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Unguarded null dereference in the new credential enumeration path.
raw_findings.impact: NullPointerException on `myUser.recoveryCodes`, aborting credential listing, whereas the sibling methods `getDisableableCredentialTypesStream` and `isConfiguredFor` guard with `myUser == null`.
raw_findings.root_cause: New method omits the null check that all other MyUser lookups in this provider perform.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add `if (myUser == null) return Stream.empty();` right after the lookup, matching the null-handling convention of the other methods in this class.
raw_findings.title: getCredentials dereferences possibly-null MyUser
raw_findings.trigger: `getCredentials` is invoked for a UserModel whose username is no longer present in the in-memory `users` map (e.g. after `removeUser` while a cached/federated UserModel is still in use).

raw_findings.body: Both methods were left OTP-only, so the deletion is a silent no-op (`log.infof("Unsupported to disable credential of type: %s")`) and the recovery-codes credential can never be removed from the user storage.

raw_findings.impact: Both methods were left OTP-only, so the deletion is a silent no-op (`log.infof("Unsupported to disable credential of type: %s")`) and the recovery-codes credential can never be removed from the user storage.
raw_findings.root_cause: Credential-type support was added to supportsCredentialType/updateCredential/isValid without the corresponding disable/remove handling.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Extend `disableCredentialType` to null out `myUser.recoveryCodes` and add `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE` to `getDisableableCredentialTypesStream` when present.
raw_findings.title: Recovery codes declared supported but never disableable/removable
raw_findings.trigger: A user with recovery codes in this storage tries to delete them (account console / admin REST), which routes to `disableCredentialType` and `getDisableableCredentialTypesStream`.

raw_findings.body: The stored list is never modified, so a recovery code stays valid forever; the new `testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin` test therefore cannot detect regressions in one-time-use semantics of user-storage-backed recovery codes.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Test double diverges from the required credential semantics, leaving the behaviour untested.
raw_findings.impact: The stored list is never modified, so a recovery code stays valid forever; the new `testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin` test therefore cannot detect regressions in one-time-use semantics of user-storage-backed recovery codes.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new validation branch implements a stateless membership check instead of one-time consumption of the recovery code.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Remove the matched code from the stored list (and persist the updated JSON) on successful validation, and extend the new test to assert that re-using the same code fails.

raw_findings.trigger: Malformed credential data stored for a user, causing `JsonSerialization.readValue` to throw IOException during credential enumeration.

raw_findings.failure_mode: Third-party providers misinterpret the credential payload format.
raw_findings.impact: The doc does not state that the `UserCredentialModel` passed to user storage carries a JSON array of *all raw* codes, while validation later passes a single raw code with the same credential type; providers can therefore be implemented with a wrong parsing contract.
raw_findings.root_cause: New public helper introduces an implicit, undocumented data format contract with user-storage providers.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Extend the javadoc to document the parameters and explicitly state that the credential value handed to user storage is a JSON array of raw recovery codes, whereas validation supplies a single raw code.

raw_findings.body: The full list of raw recovery codes is stored verbatim in `credentialData`, unlike passwords in the same provider which are hashed, and unlike local storage which stores only hashes; the sample provider therefore demonstrates an insecure storage pattern that integrators will copy.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Reference implementation persists secrets in cleartext.
raw_findings.impact: The full list of raw recovery codes is stored verbatim in `credentialData`, unlike passwords in the same provider which are hashed, and unlike local storage which stores only hashes; the sample provider therefore demonstrates an insecure storage pattern that integrators will copy.
raw_findings.root_cause: New credential branch stores the incoming challenge response (raw codes JSON) without any hashing.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Hash each code (e.g. via `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.hashRawCode`) before storing and compare hashes in `isValid`, or add an explicit comment that the cleartext storage is only acceptable for this in-memory test double.

validated_findings.body: `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user)` returns `Optional.empty()` and `credentialModelOpt.get()` throws `NoSuchElementException` while rendering the LOGIN_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES_INPUT page, producing a server error instead of the login form.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Runtime NoSuchElementException during form rendering for federated users, blocking login.
validated_findings.impact: `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user)` returns `Optional.empty()` and `credentialModelOpt.get()` throws `NoSuchElementException` while rendering the LOGIN_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES_INPUT page, producing a server error instead of the login form.
validated_findings.root_cause: The lookup was widened to federated storage (which can legitimately return no credential when the provider does not implement getCredentials) but the result is still dereferenced with an unguarded Optional.get().
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Handle the empty case explicitly, e.g. `credentialModelOpt.map(RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel::createFromCredentialModel)` and fall back to a defined codeNumber / throw a descriptive exception, instead of calling `Optional.get()` unconditionally.
validated_findings.title: Unchecked Optional.get() on recovery-codes credential in login bean
validated_findings.trigger: A federated user whose user-storage provider implements CredentialInputValidator/CredentialInputUpdater for `recovery-authn-codes` (so `isConfiguredFor` is true and the recovery-code form is shown) but leaves the *default* `CredentialInputUpdater.getCredentials()` implementation returning an empty stream, and has no local credential of that type.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Patch line R19 shows `credentialModelOpt.get()` called unconditionally after `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user)` which can return `Optional.empty()` for federated users whose provider returns empty stream from `getCredentials()`. This causes NoSuchElementException during form rendering.

validated_findings.body: `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues` never sets an id, so the exposed credential has a null id: it can never be matched for deletion, and `removeStoredCredentialById(recoveryCodeCredentialModel.getId())` in the authenticator would be invoked with null.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Credential returned from federated storage is unidentifiable, breaking id-based lookup/deletion paths.
validated_findings.impact: `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues` never sets an id, so the exposed credential has a null id: it can never be matched for deletion, and `removeStoredCredentialById(recoveryCodeCredentialModel.getId())` in the authenticator would be invoked with null.
validated_findings.root_cause: The new getCredentials() implementation rebuilds a credential model from raw values and drops the stored credential id.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: After building the model call `model.setId(myUser.recoveryCodes.getId())` (the id generated in `updateCredential`) before adding it to the returned list.
validated_findings.title: Federated recovery-codes credential is returned without an id
validated_findings.trigger: Any caller of `getFederatedCredentialsStream()` for a user whose recovery codes live in this storage, e.g. listing/deleting credentials in the account console (`CredentialDeleteHelper` filters federated credentials with `credentialId.equals(c.getId())`).
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Patch lines R237-R241 show `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues()` is called but never sets the id on the model. The stored credential has an id (line R195 shows `setId(KeycloakModelUtils.generateId())`), but `createFromValues` doesn't copy it, so returned credential has null id.

validated_findings.body: The following `authenticatedUser.credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById(...)` targets the local credential store only, so the exhausted federated credential is never removed while the required action is added; the stale credential keeps being reported as configured by the user-storage provider.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Silent no-op deletion leaving an exhausted credential in user storage.
validated_findings.impact: The following `authenticatedUser.credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById(...)` targets the local credential store only, so the exhausted federated credential is never removed while the required action is added; the stale credential keeps being reported as configured by the user-storage provider.
validated_findings.root_cause: The credential lookup was switched to include federated credentials without adapting the subsequent local-store removal call.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Only call `removeStoredCredentialById` when the credential came from local storage; for federated credentials delegate removal to the provider (e.g. `credentialManager().disableCredentialType(RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE)`), or make `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential` report the origin.
validated_findings.title: Exhausted federated recovery-codes credential removed via local-store API
validated_findings.trigger: A user whose recovery-codes credential is stored in a user-storage provider that consumes codes, logging in with the last remaining code so that `allCodesUsed()` becomes true.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Patch line R80 shows credential lookup now includes federated credentials via `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential()`, but line R86-87 still calls `removeStoredCredentialById()` which only targets local storage per `UserCredentialManager.removeStoredCredentialById()` implementation.

validated_findings.body: The stored list is never modified, so a recovery code stays valid forever; the new `testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin` test therefore cannot detect regressions in one-time-use semantics of user-storage-backed recovery codes.

validated_findings.suggested_fix: Remove the matched code from the stored list (and persist the updated JSON) on successful validation, and extend the new test to assert that re-using the same code fails.
